sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act for seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest for the injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident took place on 02112021.
2.

The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 02112021 at about 5.005.01p.m. the petitioner was riding her TVS Jupiter bearing No.KA53 ET5800 from Mittaganahalli towards Kogilu village, near Reva collegeBellahalli bridge main road, near Amulya SCCH-10 fine dine wine shop, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time, driver of the Swift car LXI bearing No.KA53N2450 came from back side with high speed, rashly and negligent manner endangering to human life without observing any traffic rules and regulation dashed against the petitioner, as a result of which petitioner fell down on the road and sustained injuries to his right leg, left hand, left leg, neck and other injuries all over the body.
3. Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Colombia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was admitted as inpatient in the said hospital and during the course of treatment xrays and CT scan were taken which reveal the fracture and on 2112021 the petitioner has been diagnosed with hairline fracture, distal radius left, C spine tenderness and underwent treatment with BE POP left wristPOP care and conservative management done and treated for the other injuries sustained in the accident, the doctor has advised SCCH-10 for followup treatment regularly and was discharged on 3112021.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/ for treatment, medicines, bed charges transportation, food and conveyance.

The petitioner was advised to take followup treatment and in this regard the petitioner is still taking followup treatment and incurred medical expense by obtaining loan from his relatives and friend.

The petitioner was hale and healthy and was very active member in the family, petitioner was aged about 26 years and was working as Veterinary doctor at Charles animal rescue centre and petitioner was earning a sum of Rs.64,500/p.m. and was unable to do work as earlier and has to take help of others to walk and do her daily work due to accidental injuries.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ from the respondents under all head together with interest and costs.
4. In response to the court notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their SCCH-10 respective counsel and filed their written statement.

5. The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 are as under:

The respondent No.1 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of petition averments in toto.
Further the respondent No.1 has denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner and injuries sustained by her and medical expenses incurred by her.

The respondent No.1 RC owner drove the Swift LXI bearing No.KA53N2450, there was a garbage truck taking a U turn and respondent was waiting as the car about to start and respondent observe all the traffic rules and start the car slowly and move the car, suddenly two wheeler bearing reg.No.KL53ET5800 came from left side and stopped in front of the respondent car and fell down and was not wearing the helmet at the time of incident and accident was caused due to the negligence of the petitioner.
The accident was occurred on SCCH-10 02112021 solely due to the negligence of the petitioner.

Further the respondent No.1 contended that he is the owner of the swift LXI car bearing reg.No.KA53N2450 and the same was insured with the respondent No.2 and the policy was in subsistence as on the date of accident.

Hence, on all these contentions,
the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition as against her.
6. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 are as under:
This respondent contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is vexatious and frivolous and also in is contrary to law and facts of the case and the petition deserves to be dismissed.
The respondent No.2 contended that, as on the date of accident the offending swift LXI car bearing reg.No.KA53N2450 was not insured with the respondent No.2 and denied the policy.
The respondent No.2 has denied the manner of accident.
The rider of the offending motorcycle has not having valid and effective driving license and violating the policy conditions.
SCCH-10
The accident was occurred on the negligence of the petitioner.
The owner and police have not complied the Sec.134 (c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The respondent No.2 submits that liability shall be as per the conditions of the insurance policy and central government rules.

Further the respondent No.2 has denied the age,
occupation and income of the petitioner and injuries sustained by the petitioner.
The respondent claim right U/Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive.
If any award is passed against the respondent the interest may be award at 6% p.a.

Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondent No.2.
7.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, she has sustained injuries in a RTA occurred on 2112021 at about 5.005.01 p.m. near Amulya Fine Dine Wine shop, Bellahalli bridge, Reva college, Bellahalli, Bridge Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and neglignet driving of the driver of Swift LXI car bearing Reg.No.KA53N2450, as alleged in the petition?

Dr.Harshitha K vs Mrs.Madhuri S.R.Cheeli on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86708950/
3 SCCH-10 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate and from whom?
3. What order or award?

8. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined herself as PW1 and got examined the M.R.O.
of Manipal hospital as PW2 and in all got marked 19 documents as ExP1 to Ex.P.19.
On the other hand, in order to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondents have not produced any oral and documentary evidence.

9. Heard the arguments and perused the records.
10.

My finding to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1: The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/
with SCCH-10 respect to the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident.

To prove the accident and the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing reg.No.KA53N2450, the petitioner herself got examined as PW1 produced documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.

Out of them the Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 are the police records like, FIR, complaint, spot sketch, Spot Mahazar, MVA report, wound certificate and charge sheet, notice u/s 133 of MV Act, reply to the police notice, discharge summary.
12. The police have investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending car for the offence punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.

The owner of the offending vehicle appeared and filed written statement and admitted that he is the owner of the insured vehicle and submits that the there was a garbage truck taking a 'U' turn and respondent was waiting as the car about to start and respondent observed all the traffic rules.
The respondent starts the SCCH-10 car and slowly move the car suddenly the petitioner ridden her motor cycle and came from the left side and stopped in front of the respondent's car and fell down.
The petitioner was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
The accident was occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 owner contended that his car is insured with respondent No.2.
Therefore, prayed to dismiss the petition.

Though respondent No.1 owner disputed the negligence on the part of the driver of her car but not stepped into witness box to prove the said fact and also not cross examined the PW1 to substantiate her defence.

The respondent No.2 insurance company has cross examined the PW1 and suggested the PW1 that as per ExP4 sketch the petitioner proceeding on the middle of the road but same has been denied by the PW1 and also suggested that the petitioner saw the garbage vehicle and to avoid the accident to the said vehicle suddenly she came on right side without Dr.Harshitha K vs Mrs.Madhuri S.R.Cheeli on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86708950/
4 indication thereby accident was occurred.
SCCH-10
The said suggestion is also denied by the petitioner/PW 1.
The petitioner has produced the notice u/s 133 of MV Act issued to the owner and reply given by the owner i.e., ExR1 as per ExP8 and 9.
The respondent No.1 in the reply notice nothing was stated about the manner of accident.

The respondent No.1 has stated manner of the accident in the objection statement but there is no substance to prove it and respondent No.1 not at all stepped into witness box to prove the manner of the accident as narrated in the written statement.
Therefore adverse inference can be drawn against respondent No.1.
Though respondent No.1 and 2 have disputed the negligence of the driver of the insured vehicle at the time of accident and they have not placed any material to prove it.
The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner shows that the accident was occurred sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA53N2450.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate, discharge summary as SCCH-10 per ExP6 and 10.
Those documents are discloses the injury and treatment.
Hence, I answer the above Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE No.2:
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident as stated above.

14. The specific contention of the petitioner that, she was proceeding on her motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA53 ET5800 and the accident was occurred on the negligence of the driver of the offending car bearing reg.No.KA53N 2450.

As a result, she has sustained grievous injury,
immediately she was shifted to the Colombia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru and she was taken treatment in the said Hospital as an inpatient.
Therefore the petitioner become disabled and lost her earning capacity.
The petitioner examined the medical record officer of Manipal hospital then Columbia asia hospital and Pw2 produced documents as per ExP16 to Ex.P19.

Ex.P16 authorization letter,
SCCH-10 Ex.P17 is the MLC Intimation, Ex.P18 is the MLC register, Ex.P19 is the case sheet.
Though MLC records and case sheets are produced by the Pw2 but he does not know the personal knowledge about the said documents.
However, the petitioner has not examined the doctor and no disability certificate is produced by the petitioner.

The petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6 and discharge summary as per Ex.P.10, aadhar card as per ExP11, DL as per ExP12,
medical bill as per ExP13, medical certificate as per ExP14, account statement as per ExP15.
On perusal of the discharge summary it shows that the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient in Colombia Asia hospital from 2112021 to 3112021.
The discharge summary discloses the discharge diagnosis as hair line fracture distal radius left.
The wound certificate and discharge summary disclose the injury and treatment.
Therefore it cannot be ignored blindly to refuse the compensation on the ground that the petitioner is not examined the doctor.

Therefore by considering the oral and documentary evidence, I am of the opinion that, the SCCH-10 petitioner has proved the accident and it has been occurred on solely negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car bearing reg.No.KA53N2450.

Therefore in view of the said accident the petitioner has sustained injury and she is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that, prior to accident she was hale and healthy, aged about 26 years and working as a doctor in Charles Animal Rescue Centre and earning of Rs.64,500/ p.m.

To support of her contention for earning the petitioner has produced the salary certificate issued by Charles Animal Rescue centre for the month of August to October 2021 and the account statement is produced as per ExP15, account statement discloses on 2122021 the amount of Rs.62,500/ was credited to the petitioner's account.
The pay slips are of August 2021 to October 2021, the account statement does not discloses the previous salary credits.
The petitioner has not examined the author of said salary slips.

Moreover the presumption cannot be drawn based on salary slips as petitioner was drawing salary of Rs.62,500/ or SCCH-10 Rs.64,500/ as the case may be because the petitioner has not proved the said salary certificate by examining the author.
Therefore in view of the nonexamination of doctor and disability certificate due to the accidental injury the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation for loss of earnings capacity.

16. The counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner has lost her leave and produced the medical certificate as per ExP14 issued by the Charlies Animal Rescue Centre and care stating that petitioner was lost the pay from December 2021, January 2022 and part of February 2022 but there is no records to prove the loss of pay by examining the author of the documents or by producing the leave grant certificate or attendance certificate.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation for loss of leave pay.
17. Though the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity, but she is entitled for medical bills and pain and sufferings.
The petitioner has produced the medical bill as SCCH-10 per Ex.P.13.
As per Ex.P.13 i.e., medical bills is of Rs.43,329/.

Though the respondents have crossexamined the petitioner and disputed about the medical bills, but the respondents have not elicited any admission from the mouth of PW1 to reject the medical medical bill under Ex.P.13.
The wound certificate as per Ex.P.6, discharge summary per Ex.P.10 as well as medical bills and nature of injury are to be considered to grant the Global compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled lumsum compensation of Rs.1,50,000/ including medical bills with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition, till the date of realization.
18. LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of objection statement as well as oral and documentary evidence, it reveals that, the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending car bearing Registration No.KA53N2450.
Further the respondent No.2 insurer has disputed the negligence of driver of the offending car but owner has SCCH-10 admitted it in reply notice as per Ex.P9.
Therefore there is no weightage in the contention of the respondents as there is a negligence of the petitioner in the accident.
19. Further, as stated above that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending car and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending motorcycle is liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,50,000/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.

6 20.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for  SCCH-10 compensation of Rs.1,50,000/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of the policy, the respondent No.2/insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, it is ordered that, the entire amount with accrued interest shall be paid to her through NEFT/RTGS by way of Epayment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
